title: Monitoring cutover & TF module stub for private deployments
content:
Purpose:
This is a working cutover playbook plus a small Terraform module sketch for private (VPC/on-prem) monitoring. Focus is on minimizing user-visible disruption while upgrading observability stacks and consolidating traffic to the centrally managed remote_write (Cortex/Thanos) endpoint. It sketches component responsibilities, TF inputs/outputs, step-by-step cutover, verification queries, and rollback criteria.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Prometheus remote_write configuration and migration patterns
- Grafana provisioning + dashboard sync in private deployments
- OTEL collector deployment patterns (daemonset vs gateway) and upgrade/rollout strategy
- Log shipping: vector/Fluent Bit sidecarless pattern and s3 batching considerations
- Terraform module interface notes for private deployments
- Cutover checklist, smoke tests, and rollback conditions

Non-goals:
- Detailed operator API docs for each downstream project (assume teams will read vendor docs)
- Full CI/CD pipeline changes (this focuses on runtime/service cutover)

Design assumptions:
- Private deployments run in k8s clusters inside customer VPCs; control plane is customer-managed but we can provision infra via TF modules that operate in the customer repo.
- Central long-term storage is Cortex/Thanos behind a secure endpoint (mTLS + IP allowlist).
- We prefer sidecarless log-forwarding in most workloads to reduce pod memory pressure; Vector daemonset will be used where sidecarless is not possible.
- Minimal schema changes to metrics (no relabeling that breaks dashboards) during cutover.

Terraform module sketch (high level):
- module "monitoring-stack" {
    source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//monitoring-private?ref=stub"
    cluster_name = var.cluster_name
    namespace = var.monitoring_namespace
    prometheus_remote_write_endpoint = var.remote_write_endpoint
    prom_tls_secret = var.prom_tls_secret  # name of k8s secret with client cert/key (mTLS)
    grafana_admin_user = var.grafana_admin_user
    grafana_provisioning_bucket = var.grafana_provisioning_bucket  # optional: S3/MinIO for dashboard provisioning
    otel_collector_mode = "daemonset"  # or "gateway"
    log_shipper = "vector"  # or "fluent-bit"
  }

Expected outputs:
- k8s_manifest_prometheus_remote_write (string) - snippet to be applied into prometheus configmap
- grafana_provisioned (bool) - indicates provisioning run completed (used for orchestration checks)
- otel_collector_deployment_name (string)

Notes on inputs: keep as few mutable variables as possible. Prefer referencing pre-existing k8s secrets for certs rather than generating in-module (avoids secret lifecycle issues during upgrades).

Implementation constraints and best practices:
- Avoid in-place relabeling of metrics that change series cardinality during cutover. If relabeling is required, do it in a canary Prometheus first.
- For remote_write, use write_shards and max_packets_per_send tuned to network MTU and customer throughput. Default conservative values in module; expose knobs.
- Grafana provisioning should be idempotent: dashboards live in a provisioning bucket (S3/MinIO) and Grafana config mounts provisioning files so upgrades are safe.
- OTEL collector: prefer a staged config where a thin gateway forwards to a small set of processors and exporters; keep queue sizes conservative to avoid memory OOMs during spikes.

Cutover plan (staged):
1) Preflight (T-7 days):
   - Confirm network egress to remote_write endpoint (CIDR allowlist) and mTLS certs work.
   - Run prometheus scrape load tests in a non-prod cluster to capture expected traffic profile.
   - Ensure Grafana provisioning bucket reachable from cluster (test with a temporary pod).
   - Inventory existing Prometheus recording rules and alerts; snapshot them and tag owners.

2) Prepare TF changes (T-5 days):
   - Add module with otel_collector_mode and remote_write config in a feature branch.
   - Configure feature-flag style toggles: prometheus.remote_write.enabled = false initially.
   - Add grafana provisioning objects to bucket and a migration dashboard set labeled "cutover-preview".

3) Canary rollout (T-3 days):
   - Deploy OTEL collector on 1-2 low-traffic nodes as daemonset with label cutover=canary. Route a subset of services to annotate endpoints for collector ingestion.
   - Deploy a canary Prometheus (same scrape configs) with remote_write.enabled = true to send to central endpoint in "dry-run" mode (if supported) or to a dedicated test tenant in Cortex/Thanos.
   - Verify metrics arrive, retention labels, and no metric explosions (check 5-min rate of new series).

4) Metrics verification (T-2 days):
   - Smoke queries (examples):
     - sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) by (service)  -> compare canary vs prod Prometheus
     - count({__name__=~".*"}) - use to detect series cardinality jumps
     - check recording rules applied and stable
   - Alert tests: trigger a low-impact alert (CPU throttling mock) and ensure it fires and recovers.

5) Partial cutover (T-1 day):
   - Flip remote_write.enabled = true for 10% of scrape configs (use relabel to select). Monitor ingestion and HA metrics in Cortex/Thanos.
   - Run log-forwarding for the same subset: point Vector daemonset configured to s3 endpoint or central log receiver. Validate end-to-end.

6) Full cutover (maintenance window):
   - Flip remote_write for remaining scrape jobs.
   - Scale up OTEL collectors to production size using autoscaling policy in TF module.
   - Remove any temporary canary Prometheus instances.

7) Post-cutover validation (0-72 hours):
   - Continuous checks: compare query latency percentiles, check for missing series with negative deltas, inspect remote_write queue metrics.
   - Validate Grafana dashboards show expected panels, and links to logs work.

Rollback criteria and steps:
- Rollback trigger (any):
  - >20% increase in cardinality persisting >30 minutes
  - Significant increase in query error rates or unacceptable query latency spikes (>2x baseline P95)
  - Alerts related to pipeline backpressure or OOMs firing repeatedly

- Rollback steps:
  1) Disable remote_write at TF module level and apply (fast rollback)
  2) Scale down OTEL collectors to previous stable replica count
  3) Re-enable old Grafana provisioning if dashboards are missing
  4) Open RCA ticket and schedule controlled reattempt once root cause fixed

Log shipping details (vector-focused):
- Prefer using a cluster-level Vector agent with per-namespace ingestion keys where possible (sidecarless). Vector ingest configuration: batch size 500–1000, timeout 5s, backoff exponential to avoid overload.
- For pods that require sidecars (legacy), keep Fluent Bit sidecars but add a relabel to drop high-cardinality metadata.
- S3 shipping: ensure chunking and compression (gzip) enabled; rotate by size (200MB) + time (10m) to balance latency vs throughput.

OTEL collector configuration guidance:
- Use receiver batch settings: send_batch_size 512, timeout 10s in gateway mode and smaller (128/5s) in daemonset mode on memory constrained nodes.
- Keep processors minimal on node collectors; complex processing (tail-based sampling, advanced filtering) should live in a small gateway cluster to reduce collector footprint.

Smoke tests (executable checklist):
- Prometheus: run predefined promql watchlist and assert values within tolerance (script returns non-zero on mismatch).
- Remote_write: validate last_success_timestamp metric and queue length < 10 for 10 minutes post-cutover.
- OTEL: verify exporter_success_count increases and exporter_error_count == 0 in first 15 minutes.
- Logs: tail last 5 minutes of logs for a canary service and assert they appear in central logger with 0 index errors.
- Grafana: provisioning status endpoint returns 200 and dashboard count >= expected.

RBAC and network considerations:
- Create a monitoring service account with minimal permissions (get/list/watch for pods, endpoints) scoped to the monitoring namespace.
- Use NetworkPolicies to restrict egress from collectors only to the permitted remote_write and log endpoints. Use egress-only subnet where possible.

Resource sizing (guideline, not prescriptive):
- Small cluster (<=50 nodes): Prometheus remote_write + gateway: 2 vCPU, 8GB per gateway replica; node collectors 0.25vCPU/256MB.
- Medium (50-200 nodes): 4 vCPU, 16GB gateway; node collectors 0.5vCPU/512MB.
- Adjust depending on scrape interval; high-cardinality metrics require more CPU for relabeling.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want to centralize all recording rules in remote_write backend or keep local recording for fast queries? (tradeoff: backend compute cost vs local query latency)
- Should TF module support in-module cert rotation or require external secret rotation?
- Do customers prefer push-mode log forwarding or pull-mode (collector scraping logs) in air-gapped setups?

Contacts / escalation:
- Primary on-call: Miguel Santos (eng-private-deployments) - +1-555-0102
- Secondary: Rina Kapoor (SRE) - +1-555-0144

Appendix: example TF snippet (usage):
module "monitoring_stack" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//monitoring-private?ref=stub"
  cluster_name = "acme-payments-prod"
  monitoring_namespace = "redwood-monitoring"
  remote_write_endpoint = "https://cortex-prod.redwood-inference.internal:9201/receive"
  prom_tls_secret = "prom-remote-mtls"
  grafana_admin_user = "grafana-admin"
  grafana_provisioning_bucket = "s3://redwood-grafana-provisioning/acme-payments-prod"
  otel_collector_mode = "gateway"
  log_shipper = "vector"
}

(End of stub)

Notes-to-self: when converting stub to real module, add acceptance tests that spin a tiny minikube cluster and validate remote_write connectivity via mock Cortex receiver.
